record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: longer exchange cycles in social-network house allocation
record.original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, what is the complexity and algorithmic structure of allowing exchange cycles longer than length 2, rather than restricting exchanges to swaps only?

evidence.quote: The most striking open question regarding exchanges in social networks involves longer cycles instead of swaps only.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $G=(N,E)$ be an undirected social network on a set $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ of agents, and let $H=\{h_1,\dots,h_n\}$ be a set of indivisible objects ("houses"). An assignment is a bijection $\sigma:N\to H$. Each agent $i\in N$ has a strict preference order $\succ_i$ over $H$. An initial assignment $\sigma_0$ is given.

For an integer $k\ge 2$, a $k$-exchange from an assignment $\sigma$ is the following operation: choose a cycle $i_1,i_2,\dots,i_\ell,i_{\ell+1}=i_1$ of distinct agents with $\ell\le k$ such that $\{i_j,i_{j+1}\}\in E$ for every $j$, and such that each agent $i_j$ strictly prefers $\sigma(i_{j+1})$ to $\sigma(i_j)$ under $\succ_{i_j}$; then form a new assignment $\sigma'$ by rotating the objects along the cycle, i.e.\ $\sigma'(i_j)=\sigma(i_{j+1})$ for $j=1,\dots,\ell$, and $\sigma'(i)=\sigma(i)$ otherwise.

A $k$-reachable assignment from $\sigma_0$ is any assignment obtained by a finite sequence of $k$-exchanges. The case $k=2$ corresponds to swaps between neighbors and has been studied extensively.

Problems. For each fixed $k\ge 3$, determine the computational complexity of the following decision problems, as a function of the structure of the social network $G$ (paths, stars, trees, cliques, general graphs, etc.):

(a) Reachable Object: given an instance $(G,H,(\succ_i)_i,\sigma_0)$, an agent $i^*\in N$, and an object $h^*\in H$, decide whether there is a $k$-reachable assignment $\sigma$ with $\sigma(i^*)=h^*$.

(b) Reachable Assignment: given an instance and a target assignment $\sigma^*$, decide whether $\sigma^*$ is $k$-reachable from $\sigma_0$.

(c) Pareto-Efficient Reachable Assignment: decide whether there exists a $k$-reachable assignment from $\sigma_0$ that is Pareto-efficient among all $k$-reachable assignments, and if so, design an algorithm to find one.

Provide a complete complexity classification (polynomial-time algorithms or hardness results) for these problems when exchange cycles of length up to $k>2$ are permitted, generalizing what is known for the swap-only case $k=2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The swap (length-2) version on social networks has been studied with complexity results for various graph classes (paths, stars, trees, cliques), but the literature treats extension to longer exchange cycles as an open direction; no comprehensive complexity classification for $k\ge 3$ appears in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Object Allocation via Swaps along a Social Network
status_evidence.snippet: Allocations emerging from a sequence of simple swaps between pairs of neighbors in a social network; complexity studied for reachability, obtaining a given object, Pareto-efficiency, with polynomial and NP-complete cases.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work focuses on length-2 swaps; longer cycle generalization is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Object Reachability via Swaps under Strict and Weak Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies reachability via swaps along edges of a social network.
status_evidence.claim: Continuing line of work restricted to swaps, leaving longer exchange cycles open.

status_evidence.title: Housing Market on Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Mechanisms restricted to swaps with neighbors or constrained trading cycles.
status_evidence.claim: General longer-cycle exchanges on social networks remain a separate, less-explored model.
